I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. I have about 8 mu of flat, loamy ground on the North China Plain. There's really only one thing to do here — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what everyone does. That's what the land is good for. I know this rotation inside out.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after the summer corn is off the field. I'll rotary till first — the soil needs loosening after the corn roots and the summer heat. I'll buy improved seed from the supply station in town, the Jimai variety has been good to me. I'll put down a compound fertilizer at planting — phosphorus and potassium in the base application — then top-dress with urea around jointing stage in late March when the plants need a push. I irrigate four times: once before winter to help the roots settle, once at jointing, once at heading, once at grain fill. I spray herbicide in winter before the weeds take hold, then I'll hit the aphids and powdery mildew in May. I expect 450 jin to the mu on a normal year.

Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant maize directly into the stubble — no till, no time to waste. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar, from the county seed shop. The summer rains usually do most of the work, but I'll irrigate twice if the sky is stingy. Corn needs nitrogen more than anything — I'll apply it in two shots, at planting and at the big bell stage. One herbicide pass right after emergence, maybe one more spray if the corn borer shows up bad. Harvest in late September.

I'm 55. My back isn't what it was. I stick to what I know works. I'm not experimenting with anything new this year.
